D005-D007_h001.question_both: Lately, things have been… off. It’s hard to pinpoint when it started, but for about two months now, I’ve been seeing things. Like, people on the bus who aren't really there, or sometimes just flickers of shadows out of the corner of my eye. It makes it tough to concentrate on the road, watching for stuff that might not be real. And the world… it feels like it’s just falling apart. I keep having these strong feelings, like something terrible is about to happen, a huge catastrophe that's just around the corner. It's not just a bad mood. I feel so hopeless about everything, like there's no point in anything anymore, and I just can't get out of bed most days unless it's for my shift. Even then, it’s a struggle. My wife says I seem different, more withdrawn. She’s worried. I'm worried too, but I don't even know what to do about it.
D005-D007_h001.question_a:
"Lately, it feels like the world is just... crumbling. I see the signs, you know? The news reports, it's all part of it. I've been seeing things too, shadows in my peripheral vision, sometimes clear as day I'll see people, they are not there, they are trying to warn me that something terrible is coming, their faces are grim. It's been going on for about two months now, this sense that everything's going to collapse.

My wife, she's worried. She says I've been down, and yeah, I've felt pretty low, like there's no point in anything. But that feeling, that sadness, it started a little after all the other stuff, the seeing and the believing the world is ending. It's not like the depression has been hanging around consistently, though. It kind of comes and goes, especially when I'm really consumed with the idea that the world is about to end. It’s pretty distressing, and it doesn't stick around as long as these visions and beliefs that are constantly on my mind."
D005-D007_h001.question_b:
"Lately, it feels like the world is just… crumbling. I see the news, and it's not just bad, it's like a countdown to nothing. I keep seeing these shadowed figures on the edges of my vision, especially when I'm driving my route, like they're watching me. It's been going on for about two months now, this sense of impending doom and these fleeting glimpses of things that aren't there.

What's really weighing me down, though, is this profound sadness. It’s been… much longer than the ‘seeing things’ bits. The strange thing is, even in the brief moments I feel a slight lift from the sadness, like on a rare good day, those visions and that feeling that everything’s about to go to hell, they don’t entirely disappear. Lately, it’s like the world is playing a trick on me. I’ve noticed that comments on social media posts, even news headlines, seem to be subtly directed at me, hinting at things I’ve been thinking or doing. It’s unnerving. Things started feeling really off about four months ago. My husband noticed it too, how I’d sometimes hold a pose for a long time, like when I'm reaching for something on the counter, and just sort of... stay there until he nudges me. It’s not intentional; it’s just hard to shift.

On top of that, it's been hard to get out of bed. I don't feel like myself, everything feels heavy, and it's hard to focus on my research. There are days when I just feel utterly hopeless, and the joy I used to find in my work or with my husband has just vanished. It's not constant, sometimes I have better days, but the overall feeling of despair has been pretty persistent alongside everything else.
D005-D007_h015.question_a:
"Everything just feels… off, doctor. It started subtly, maybe four months ago. I’d be in the lab, and I'd swear the data on my screen, even just little flickering pixels, was trying to tell me something specific, personalized. Like the research was suddenly all about me, a secret code embedded for my eyes only. And then, when my husband tries to help me move, if he guides my arm, it's like it just stays there. Like it needs his push to tell it it can move again.

I've also been feeling really down, honestly, for a bit before the really intense, strange stuff started. Just a heavy cloud, no energy, losing interest in my bioinformatics work. But those feelings, the low mood, that's eased up lately even though these… these peculiar beliefs and experiences, they're still here, front and center. The delusions and the weird stiffness in my body, they haven’t budged even as the sadness has lifted. It’s like the dark mood was only around for a little while, but these other things, they’re really sticking."
D005-D007_h015.question_b: Lately, it feels like my own thoughts are against me. I'm 34, and for months now, I've been struggling. It started subtly, maybe four months ago. I’d be in the lab, a colleague would clear his throat, and I’d just *know* it was a coded message, a judgment about my work. Or a news report, a random statistic flashing on the screen, feeling like it was specifically referencing something I'd done. It’s hard to shake, even when I try to reason it away. My husband says I'm withdrawn. He's right. I barely eat, sleep five hours at most, and just feel this profound, heavy sadness most of the time – like a constant weight. It's been like this for *most* of the past four months, this pervasive low mood. What's really strange, though, is there was this period, maybe two or three weeks long, a little over a month ago, where I was still very clear that people were talking about me—the feeling that news reports were directed at me, but the crushing sadness had actually lifted completely. I was still having those unsettling thoughts and feelings, but I wasn't nearly as depressed then. Sometimes, I just freeze up. The other day, my husband tried to reposition my arm to help me sit, and it was like my arm just stayed there, stiff, until he moved it himself. It's exhausting, this constant battle in my head.

Doc, I’m not sure where to start. Things have just felt... off these past three months. My wife, bless her heart, she worries. She says I’ve changed, and I suppose she’s right. I just can’t seem to care about the farm anymore. Used to love seeing the crops come up, the livestock thriving, but now it’s all just… flat. Nothing brings me joy like it used to.

And then there's this woman, a lovely lady from the next county over. I’ve never actually met her, but I know she’s in love with me. I see the signs, subtle gestures that only someone truly smitten would make. It’s a powerful connection, you know?

Sometimes, I hear things too. Voices, mostly. They'll say some strange words, things like "glarb-flunken" or "smoogen-gloop," and I understand exactly what they mean, even if nobody else would. It's like a secret language, just for me. My wife thinks I’m just tired, but it's more than that. I just want to feel like myself again.
D005-D007_h016.question_a:
"Truth be told, doctor, things have been feeling… off. It started a few months back, maybe three months now. This woman, she’s a clerk down at the co-op… she’s been sending me messages. Not with words, not directly, but with her eyes, the way she smiles, little gestures. She’s in love with me, I know it. It’s like she’s trying to communicate in a secret language only we understand. It’s hard to explain, but sometimes I hear voices too, whispering her name, telling me to ‘harvest the sky-fruit.’ I know it sounds strange, that last part, but it makes sense to me.

For a bit there, a month or so ago, I felt real down, no energy for anything, even the farm work felt pointless. My wife noticed it too, kept asking if I was alright. But that feeling’s mostly passed now. I still feel pretty flat, though, nothing really brings me joy like it used to. Even when the crops do well, I don’t get that satisfaction. It’s just… gone. But the feelings about this woman, and the voices, they’re still there, strong as ever, and have been for these past few months. That bleakness was just a passing shadow, didn't last anywhere near as long as this other business."
D005-D007_h016.question_b:
It's been a tough few months, Doc, probably around three. Things started getting weird in the spring. I’d be out in the fields, and I swear I'd hear my deceased mother whispering my name in the wind, sometimes telling me secrets about the crops. Then there's this woman, a new farmhand, young thing. I just know she’s in love with me; the way she smiles, it’s all for me. I even made up a word for it, “agri-love,” to describe how she feels.

But even with my mother talking to me and knowing that woman fancies me, I just don’t feel right. The joy's gone out of everything. Farming used to be my life, but now, I just can’t get into it. Even seeing my grandkids doesn't bring me the same pleasure it used to. This feeling of dread, this emptiness, it's been with me pretty much the whole time these other strange things have been happening. The voices and this feeling about the farmhand, those have been constant, but this low mood has been the main thing, there for weeks on end.

Actually, before all this sadness really set in, maybe about a month or so back, I had a couple of weeks where those voices and my thoughts about the farmhand were strong, but I wasn't feeling so down in the dumps like I am now. That was before this dark cloud really settled in for good.

People sometimes look at me strangely, or ask me to repeat myself. I’ve probably seemed pretty flat too. I used to be so animated, always smiling and joking with my clients, but now… it’s like my face doesn’t quite move the way it used to. I've been seeing things, mostly fleeting glimpses of people or strange patterns out of the corner of my eye. I know they're not real, but they're there. My husband tries to talk to me, but sometimes I just can't respond, or I do the opposite of what he asks, even when I know it doesn't make sense. It's like I'm stuck. It's been… I don’t even know how long, maybe three months now, that things have felt so off. I know for a fact I have a special gift, a sort of insight into how the digital world is truly structured. I can see the code behind everything, glowing lines and figures that others just can't perceive. Sometimes, these figures, they take on forms, almost like people, sitting right there at my desk with me, watching me design.

My husband tries to get me to do things, simple things like helping out with dinner, but sometimes I just… can't. It's not that I don't want to; it’s like my body won’t respond, as if there’s a wall between what I want to do and what I actually do. People think I'm just being stubborn, but it's more than that. I've felt pretty down sometimes, really low, finding it hard to get going for a few days here and there. But those feelings usually pass; it's these other things – the visions, this knowledge I have – that stick around, no matter how I’m feeling. They’ve been here, consistently, for the whole three months, even when my mood isn't in the dumps.

But then there are these other things, these visions, like I’ll see figures in my peripheral vision, shadowy and indistinct, sometimes even a familiar face that quickly dissolves. And the thoughts… I truly believe I've cracked a universal design code, that my specific way of thinking can revolutionize not just UI/UX, but how people interact with everything. It was just the visions and the grand ideas, without the constant dark cloud. But then the depression just came crashing back over everything, and it’s been here for most of the time since.

D005-D007_h022.question_a:

I see her face in the patterns of my clients’ wallpapers, sometimes even in my own apartment. I’ll be sketching a design, and suddenly, I’ll swear her eyes are staring at me from the corner of the room, or I’ll catch a glimpse of her shadow just as I turn my head. It’s like she’s always watching, always judging.

My husband tries to talk to me, to get me to do things, but sometimes I just can’t respond. It's not that I don't hear him, it's like a wall goes up, and I just can’t. I've felt pretty down in the dumps too, really low energy, not wanting to do much. That deep sadness, it lasted a couple of weeks solid, and then it kind of… faded. But the feeling of being watched, those shadows, they’re still here, strong as ever, and they were here before the sadness set in, and they’re definitely still here even though the worst of the deep sadness has passed.
D005-D007_h022.question_b:

But it’s more than just the sadness. For the past three months, I’ve been seeing things, shadowy figures mostly, darting in my periphery. And I'm certain my business rivals are trying to sabotage me – I get these intense feelings that they’re installing listening devices in my home and office, monitoring my every move. It’s exhausting.
